_meta.purpose: Retort project benchmark findings ingested as routing heuristics for the ADR-2080 model-router console. These are EXTERNAL measurements from adrianco/retort (Adrian Cockcroft), not our own benchmarks — we trust the ranking, not the absolute numbers.
_meta.methodology: Controlled factorial experiments: language × model × effort × prompt methodology. Easy task = REST API CRUD (bookshop); hard task = Brazilian-soccer MCP server (12 capabilities). 13 languages, 258+ scored runs. Key metric: requirement_coverage (binary 1.00 or fail), plus code_quality, test_coverage, defect_rate, maintainability, cost_usd, duration_seconds.
_meta.caveat_agent_vs_api: All costs are AGENT-LEVEL (total per-run including all API calls in the agentic loop), not raw per-token API costs. codex agents stay terse (10-19 turns regardless of effort); claude-code agents scale with effort (15-140 turns). This makes per-token list price a poor proxy for per-task cost.
_meta.caveat_judge_bias: Retort uses its own scoring rubric; absolute scores are not directly comparable to the ruflo seed corpus judge (Sonnet 4.6 LLM-judged 5-criterion rubric). Trust the RANKING and cost ratios, not absolute quality numbers.

effort_cost_scaling.description: Same routine task (1.00 coverage everywhere) — how cost scales with effort level. Key finding: codex/Terra stays FLAT, claude-code/Opus explodes.
effort_cost_scaling.explanation: Terra/codex uses 10-19 agent turns regardless of effort; Opus/claude-code scales from 15 to 140 turns. Agent verbosity is the dominant cost driver, not per-token price.

routing_heuristics.h1_routine_cheapest_wins: For routine/easy tasks all tested models achieve 1.00 requirement_coverage. Optimise purely for cost: local > Terra > Astra > Claude tiers. Leave effort at LOW — proven-reliable work matches max-effort reliability at a fraction of cost.
routing_heuristics.h2_hard_fable_over_opus: For hard/complex tasks Fable 5 matches Opus 5 reliability (both 1.00) at 40% of the cost ($10.47 vs $26.48). Prefer Fable for hard tasks unless Opus-specific capabilities are needed.
routing_heuristics.h3_budget_hard_sonnet: Budget-constrained hard tasks: Sonnet 5 at 0.93 pass rate for $7.64 is the best reliability-per-dollar trade-off.
routing_heuristics.h4_language_not_model: Language choice drives code quality (94-96% of variance), NOT model choice. Model drives requirement_coverage (reliability). Do not upgrade model tier for 'better code' — that is wasted money.
routing_heuristics.h5_fast_mode_routine_only: Fast mode (Opus 4.8 vs 4.7) gives 20-40% speed gain on routine tasks but 26-48% cost increase, and NO speed gain on hard tasks. Use only when a human is waiting on routine work.
routing_heuristics.h6_agent_verbosity_multiplier: Agent architecture dominates cost more than per-token price. codex stays terse at any effort; claude-code token usage scales superlinearly with effort. A $50/M-token model via a terse agent can be cheaper per task than a $3/M-token model via a verbose agent.
routing_heuristics.h7_tdd_free_quality: TDD prompting is a nearly-free quality knob for cloud models. ATDD actively hurts local models.
routing_heuristics.h8_repair_amplifies_not_creates: Self-repair loops double local model pass rates for languages the model partially knows; zero improvement on unsupported languages. Repair amplifies competence, does not create it.
